messages.author: 9ad695e063ae4c4f
messages.subject: How to speed up my stan code?
parts:
hello,

The following paragraph is my stan code.
I ran 2-chain with 2-cores and iteration 150000 times.
It took around 69 hrs.
I really want to know how can I speeding up my code.
Thank you.

 data
{
int <lower=0> n;//206
int <lower=0> N;//2695
cov_matrix[3] S;
vector<lower=0>[n] stage;//early stage and advanced stage
int<lower=0> ID[N];
vector[N] observetime;
vector[N] log10ca125;
}

parameters
{
real u1; // sigma
real<lower=0> u2; // sigma_stage
real u11; // beta1
real<lower=0> u12; // beta1_stage
real beta2; //beta2
real beta3; //beta3
real delta; //skewness parameters of random error
vector[3] deltab; //skewness parameters of random effect
matrix<lower=0>[n,3]  wb; //wb = |X_0b|~|N(0,1)|
cov_matrix[3] cov;
matrix[n,3] b; //random effect 
real<lower=3> nu; //degree of freedom
vector<lower=0>[n] ue; //latent random variables generated by ST distribution 
vector<lower=0>[N] w;
vector[N] Y_pred;
}
transformed parameters
{
vector[n] beta1; // Stage info for extra random effects mean
vector<lower=0>[n] sigma; // Standard deviation
matrix[n,3] mub;//mean of random effect matrix
real d1;
real<lower=0> mue;
//----------------------------------------
vector[n] p1;
vector[n] p2;
vector[n] p3;
//----------------------------------------
vector[N] dm;
vector[N] mu;
vector[N] aau;
vector[N] res;
vector[N] sue;
real sten;
//----------------------------------------
beta1 = u11 + u12 * stage;
sigma = exp(u1 + u2 * stage);
for(i in 1:3)
{
mub[,i] = deltab[i] * (wb[,i] - sqrt(2/3.14159));
}
//means of error term (ST distribution)
mue = exp(lgamma(0.5*(nu-1)) -lgamma(0.5*nu))*sqrt(nu/3.14159);
d1 = nu/2;
sten = sqrt(10);

// Mixture of nonlinear mixed-effects models with two components using ST distribution 
p1 = beta1 + b[,1];
p2 = beta2 + b[,2];
p3 = beta3 + b[,3];
 
sue = sqrt(ue[ID]);
aau = sue .* sigma[ID];
dm = ( p1[ID] + p2[ID] .* observetime + p3[ID] .* observetime .* observetime)/log(10);
mu = dm + delta*(w-mue);
res = log10ca125 - mu;

}
//----------------------------------------
model
{
//degree of freedom
nu ~ exponential(0.1);

// Linear regression
u1 ~ normal(0,sten);
u2 ~ normal(0,sten);
u11 ~ normal(0,sten);
u12 ~ normal(0,sten);

//skewness parameters 
  delta ~ normal(0,sten);  //random error 
  deltab ~ normal(0,sten); //random effect 

//Random effects of response model
for(i in 1:3)
wb[,i] ~ normal(0,1);
//Variance-covariance matrix
  cov ~ inv_wishart(3,S);
//random effect
for(s in 1:n)
b[s,] ~ multi_normal(mub[s,],cov);

//Latent random variables generated by ST distribution 
  ue ~ inv_gamma(d1,d1);
w ~ normal(0,sue);

//Coefficients 
beta2 ~ normal(0,sten);
beta3 ~ normal(0,sten);

//Generate ST random variable y from the SN tandom variable z.
log10ca125 ~ normal(mu, aau);
Y_pred ~ normal(mu, aau);

}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to speed up my stan code?
parts:
First, you probably don't need 150K iterations with NUTS.

Vectorize the multi-normal.

> for(s in 1:n)
> b[s,] ~ multi_normal(mub[s,],cov);

as

b ~ multi_normal(mub, cov);

That means you have to declare b and mub as

vector[3] b[n];

and

vector[3] mub[n];

We recommend a scaled correlation matrix parameterized with
a Cholesky factor---it's much more efficient. We don't yet
have very efficient Wisharts and inverse Wisharts, but we
will might eventually if someone writes the Cholesky-factor
parameter versions.

And vectorize

> for(i in 1:3)
> wb[,i] ~ normal(0,1);

as

to_vector(wb) ~ normal(0, 1);

If you don't care about all those transformed parameters, just
make them local variables in the model. Then they won't
get saved. 150K draws might take a lot of memory if n is large
and you save all those transforms.

- Bob

We don't know of any models where JAGS/BUGS converge but Stan
doesn't, so my first guess is that the models are not the same.

Did you run multiple chains from random starting points in WinBUGS?
I'm not sure what it does by default to test convergence, but Stan's
tests are more stringent by design.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to speed up my stan code?
parts:
Nothing should be taking 150000 iterations.  I can't be sure but I'm guessing there are big problems with your model if it's needing so many iterations.  The model seems simple enough that I can't see why it wouldn't converge after 2000 iterations!

Also, just a minor thing:  in Stan we have pi().  And sqrt(2/pi) can be computed in the transformed data block.  But I think there must be some simple problems with your model somewhere (in Bugs or Stan).

A

The scale of data is around 0 to 5.
